detail:
<p>Vancouver, WA — At approximately 4:30 p.m., the Vancouver Fire Department responded to a report of a vehicle into a building at an apartment complex off SE 139th Ave.</p>

<p>Engine 8 arrived first and secured the vehicle, which was not running, and assisted the occupant with extrication. The individual was able to exit under their own power and was transported by AMR to a local hospital. The extent of injuries is unknown at this time. One person who lives at the apartment complex was displaced as a result of the incident.&nbsp; Damage costs are unknown. The Vancouver Fire Department’s coordinated response ensured scene safety and minimized further impact to the residents.</p>

detail:

<p><strong>FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:&nbsp;</strong>Feb. 4, 2026</p>

<p><strong>Media&nbsp;Contact:&nbsp;</strong><a href="mailto:communications@employ.oregon.gov" target="_blank">communications@employ.oregon.gov</a></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-size:20px"><strong>WorkSource Oregon&nbsp;to Host&nbsp;Second Chance Career Fair in Southeast Portland</strong></span></p>

<p style="text-align: center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>PORTLAND, Ore.</strong>&nbsp;—&nbsp;WorkSource Oregon&nbsp;will&nbsp;host&nbsp;its first-ever&nbsp;Second Chance Career Fair&nbsp;on Wednesday, Feb.11,&nbsp;from 10 a.m. to noon at the WorkSource Oregon – Portland Metro Southeast Center in Portland.&nbsp;The&nbsp;free&nbsp;event will&nbsp;connect&nbsp;job seekers with local&nbsp;employers&nbsp;who are&nbsp;open&nbsp;to hiring&nbsp;people&nbsp;facing&nbsp;barriers to employment, including recent incarceration.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“This event is about opening doors,” Oregon Employment Department director Andrew R. Stolfi&nbsp;said. “We want job seekers to have direct conversations with employers who value skills, potential, and growth, and who understand that talent exists everywhere.”&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>All job seekers are invited to attend and connect with&nbsp;employers&nbsp;from a range of industries,&nbsp;including healthcare, social services, manufacturing, staffing, and nonprofit organizations. Employers and community partners scheduled to&nbsp;attend include the City of Portland, Dress for Success, Gliss, Central City Concern, United Salad, Stone Soup, DPI Staffing, The Pathfinder Network, Urban League of Portland, and Oxford House.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“We encourage attendees to bring copies of their resumes and be prepared to speak directly with employers about current job openings, career pathways, and next steps,” said Reentry Specialist Chelsea Cook, who is coordinating the job fair. “WorkSource&nbsp;Oregon&nbsp;staff will also&nbsp;be available to&nbsp;provide information about job search support and employment services.” Cook specializes in helping people who have been formerly incarcerated find jobs.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>This is the first time WorkSource&nbsp;Oregon&nbsp;has&nbsp;hosted a&nbsp;career fair focused on&nbsp;second chance&nbsp;hiring&nbsp;but&nbsp;hopes&nbsp;to&nbsp;make&nbsp;it an annual event in the future.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>Event details</strong>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>Date:</strong>&nbsp;Wednesday, Feb. 11, 2026&nbsp;<br />
<strong>Time:</strong>&nbsp;10 a.m. to noon&nbsp;<br />
<strong>Location:</strong>&nbsp;WorkSource Oregon – Portland Metro Southeast Center&nbsp;<br />
6401 SE Foster Rd., Portland,&nbsp;OR 97206&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>Email: </strong><a href="mailto:EmployerServices@oregon.gov" target="_blank">EmployerServices@oregon.gov</a>.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>About&nbsp;Workforce Operations</strong>&nbsp;</p>

<p>The Oregon Employment Department’s Workforce Operations division is a partner in WorkSource Oregon, a consortium of state agencies and local workforce boards, and&nbsp;operates&nbsp;37 WorkSource Oregon centers across the state. WorkSource Oregon offers a wide range of free services&nbsp;to job seekers,&nbsp;employers,&nbsp;and businesses, including&nbsp;personalized career coaching, resume writing, job search strategies,&nbsp;support for job postings&nbsp;and&nbsp;hiring incentives, and access to labor-market data. Visit&nbsp;<a href="https://worksourceoregon.org/">worksourceoregon.org</a>&nbsp;for more information.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<hr />
<p>WorkSource Oregon (WSO) is an equal opportunity agency. WSO provides free help so you can use our services. Some examples are sign language and spoken-language interpreters, written materials in other languages, large print, audio, and other formats. To get help, please call 503-947-1680. TTY users call 711. You can also send an email to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EmployerServices@oregon.gov" target="_blank">EmployerServices@oregon.gov.</a>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>WorkSource&nbsp;Oregon (WSO) es una agencia de igualdad de oportunidades. WSO proporciona ayuda gratuita para que usted pueda utilizar nuestros servicios. Algunos ejemplos son intérpretes de lengua de señas e idiomas hablados, materiales escritos en otros idiomas, letra grande, audio y otros formatos. Para obtener ayuda, por favor llame al 503-947-1680. Usuarios de TTY pueden llamar al 711. También puede enviar un correo electrónico&nbsp;a&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EmployerServices@oregon.gov" target="_blank">EmployerServices@oregon.gov</a>.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Media Contact: &nbsp;<a href="mailto:Communications@employ.oregon.gov">Communications@employ.oregon.gov;</a> <a href="https://stateoforegon.sharepoint.com/sites/OED-Communications-Cross-DivisionCommunications/Shared%20Documents/Media%20-%20Agency%20Level/Robin.Maxey@dor.oregon.gov">Robin.Maxey@dor.oregon.gov</a></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align: center;"><strong><span style="font-size:20px">WorkSource Oregon, Department of Revenue team up to provide free tax help events</span>&nbsp;</strong></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>SALEM, Ore</strong>. —&nbsp;Oregon taxpayers can get free help filing their federal and state personal income tax returns electronically at six different WorkSource Oregon locations across the state in February and March.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>WorkSource Oregon and the Oregon Department of Revenue are teaming up to provide the assistance. Volunteers from Revenue will be stationed at local WorkSource Oregon centers to help guide taxpayers through the filing process using the free public-access computers and Wi-Fi internet service.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>The first event is planned for Wednesday, February 18, at the WorkSource center at 120 E Lincoln, Suite 115b, in Woodburn. Other events are planned in Hillsboro, Eugene, southeast Portland, Lebanon, and Bend.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“WorkSource Oregon centers are trusted community spaces where Oregonians come to find jobs, build skills, and get connected to services,” said Andrew R. Stolfi, director of the Oregon Employment Department, which is a partner of WorkSource Oregon. “Partnering with the Department of Revenue to offer free tax filing assistance is a natural extension of our customer-service mission. We are thrilled to help Oregonians get support in filing their taxes, claiming the credits they’ve earned, and keeping more money in their pockets.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“We know that filing your taxes can be a scary and confusing process. We are excited to partner with WorkSource Oregon to provide in person help to make it easier for Oregonians to file their taxes for free, check if they are eligible for refundable tax credits like the Earned Income Tax Credit or Oregon Kids Credit, and claim their share of the kicker,” said David Gerstenfeld, Department of Revenue director.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>WorkSource Oregon is a statewide partnership with the Oregon Employment Department and state, local, and nonprofit agencies. WorkSource provides a variety of employment and training services to job seekers and employers in Oregon, helping people find jobs and businesses find talent.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>Taxpayers are encouraged to set up a Revenue Online account through the Department of Revenue’s website before coming to an event if they plan to use Direct File Oregon. They should bring tax information with them, including:<br />
&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
     <li>Social security number or ITIN for everyone on their tax return</li>
     <li>Forms W-2 (wages from a job)</li>
     <li>Forms 1099-G, 1099-R, 1099-INT (other income) if applicable</li>
     <li>Form SSA-1099 (Social Security Benefits)</li>
     <li>Bank routing and account numbers for direct deposit (can be found on their checks)</li>
     <li>Last year’s tax return</li>
</ul>

<hr />
<p><br />
The Oregon Employment Department (OED) provides economic stability to Oregon communities by providing vital services to both businesses and workers.&nbsp;OED supports businesses with finding qualified job candidates, labor market information, tax incentives and support, and retaining talent through economic downturns. OED promotes employment through wage replacement benefits during unemployment and significant life events, job placement, training, and useful career information. Learn more at <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Pages/default.aspx">employment.oregon.gov</a>.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>OED’s Workforce Operations division is a partner in WorkSource Oregon, a consortium of state agencies and local workforce boards, and operates 37 WorkSource Oregon centers across the state. WorkSource Oregon offers a wide range of free services, including personalized career coaching, resume writing, interview practice, and job search strategies. For employers and businesses, WorkSource Oregon provides support for job postings and finding qualified candidates, hiring incentives, and access to labor-market data – all at no cost. Visit <a href="https://www.worksourceoregon.org/">worksourceoregon.org</a> for more information.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>To get tax forms, check the status of their refund, or make tax payments, taxpayers can visit the <a href="http://www.oregon.gov/dor">Department of Revenue website</a> or email <a href="mailto:questions.dor@oregon.gov">questions.dor@oregon.gov</a>. Taxpayers can also call 800-356-4222 toll-free from an Oregon prefix (English or Spanish) or 503-378-4988 in Salem and outside Oregon. For TTY (hearing- or speech-impaired), the Department of Revenue accepts all relay calls.</p>
